text: {"question":"How does the greater precision of helium abundance measurements relative to deuterium influence the effectiveness of BBN constraints in addressing the Hubble tension for cosmological models that tend to favor higher values of the baryon density parameter Ω_b h^2?","reference_answer":"Because helium measurements are twice as precise as current deuterium data, they provide a tighter constraint on the baryon density. This tighter bound limits the ability of models that push Ω_b h^2 upward to alleviate the Hubble tension, making BBN constraints from helium more effective than deuterium in ruling out such solutions."}
